competences: The learner identifies key facts about the constitutions of uganda.
The learner explains information about The 1962, 1967 and 1995 constitutions using reference texts.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, spells, reads and writes constitution, 1962, 1967, 1995.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify facts about the constitutions of uganda.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer the available sourced questions about The 1962, 1967 and 1995 constitutions.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied Uganda and related Social Studies concepts. They build on this earlier work to learn about the constitutions of uganda.
materials: Chart showing the constitutions of uganda
Primary Five SST reference on The 1962, 1967 and 1995 constitutions
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous SST topic and introduces the constitutions of uganda. They ask "Why is 8 th October 1995 remembered in the political history of Uganda?" and listen to learners' first responses before referring to the source notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied content and answer the opening question, explaining their ideas in short sentences.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about the constitutions of uganda
steps.content: The 1962 constitution which led Uganda to independence . It made provisions for the position of the president and the prime minister. It replaced the 1995 constitution Qn: Why was the 1995 constitution referref to as the people’s It was the day when the 1995 constitution was made known to the public /Launched This was the constitution which led Uganda to independence. It was replaced by the 1966 constitution. It replaced the 1962 constitution The 1995 constitution is different from other constitutions because it was made by people from all parts of Uganda. The work of the CADS was to debate and finish the 1995 constitution. The 1995 constitution was launched on 8 th October 1995 at the constitutional square.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about the constitutions of uganda on the chalkboard, including "The 1962 constitution which led Uganda to independence . It made provisions for the position of the president and the prime minister.; It replaced the 1995 constitution Qn: Why was". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Further facts about the constitutions of uganda
steps.content: The president was given more powers to rule the country than the prime minister. (iv) The 1995 constitution. Dr. Milton Obote used the 1966 constitution to abolish kingdoms in 1967. This constitution is also called the republic constitution because it declared Uganda a republic. In 1993 the constituent Assembly was set up to make the new constitution for Uganda. The CA was made up of people from all over Uganda. They were called CADS- Constitution Assembly Delegates. He chaired the constitutional Commission which collected views from all Ugandans. steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original questions, starting with "Why is 8 th October 1995 remembered in the political history of Uganda?" and "What was the weakness of 1962 constitution?". They monitor pupils as they answer, check responses against the source material and provide corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise questions independently, consult their copied notes and correct any mistakes after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the factual content on the constitutions of uganda, asks "Why is 8 th October 1995 remembered in the political history of Uganda?" and follows up with "What was the weakness of 1962 constitution?". They confirm the answers and assign the remaining sourced practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners state one important fact from their lesson notes, answer the final oral questions and correct their written work.

assessment: Use the original questions "Why is 8 th October 1995 remembered in the political history of Uganda?" and "What was the weakness of 1962 constitution?", along with other listed items, to assess learners' understanding and correct errors from the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining sourced question, including "Who were the constituent assemblies delegated?"
